texts.preamble: Mohammed Mustkim vs Urban Administration And Development ... on 15 January, 2018 -: 1 :- High Court Of Madhya Pradesh; Bench At Indore Writ Petition No.3139 of 2017. (Mohammed Mustkim and others v/s State of M.P. and others) Indore, Dated : 15.01.2018:-
texts.facts: THE petitioners have filed the present petition being aggrieved by the notices dated 03.05.2017 issued by the Respondent No.5 [2] The petitioners are the permanent residents of Neemuch are engaged in the business of sale of Chicken/Mutton/Fish since last 100 years. According to them they have obtained licenses to sell Chicken/Mutton/Fish through shops from the Competent Authority in the year 2012 and all were renewed for the next year also. The Municipal Council, Neemuch has also granted permission to the petitioners to run their shops and no objection certificate was issued by Chief Municipal Officer, Municipal Council, Neemuch. In the year 2014 the petitioners had submitted application for renewal of license and also deposited the necessary fees before the Competent Authority and the said application has been rejected by the Competent Authority. Again on 11.01.2017 the petitioners have submitted application for renewal of the said license by completing all the formalities but instead of renewing the license the Respondent No.5 has issued notices on 03.05.2017 directing them to stop the sell of Chicken/Mutton/Fish within 3 days for want of necessary license. After receiving the said notices, the petitioners submitted the objections before the authority and also reminder for renewal of their license for which their applications are pending since January, 2017 when no head was given then all petitioners approached this court by way of the present writ petition under article 226 of the Constitution Of India . [3] The petitioners have assailed the impugned notices on the ground that before issuing such notices no opportunity of hearing was given to them . The petitioners are having no objection certificate issued by the Respondent No.5 and on the basis of such no objection certificate necessary licenses were issued to them. The petitioners are having fundamental right to do the business to earn livelihood,therefore, the impugned notices are illegal, void and liable to be set-aside. [4] After notice, the Respondent Nos.2, 3 and 4 filed their brief reply by submitting that as per Clause 1.1 of Food Safety and Standard Regulation, 2011, the petitioners are not permitted to sell Chicken/Mutton/Fish without necessary license and no objection certificate from the local Mohammed Mustkim vs Urban Administration And Development ... on 15 January, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31428181/ 1 authority. Since as on today the petitioners are not having the license and no objection certificate from the Municipal Council, they have no right to sell.
texts.arguments: [5] The Respondent No.5 being a contesting party to this case has also filed its reply raising preliminary objection that in order to do the business of sell of Chicken/Mutton/Fish a valid license under Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006 is statutorily required and admittedly the petitioners are not having the valid license since September, 2014. Therefore, they cannot be permitted to run the business. The petitioners are selling the Chicken/Mutton/Fish in a densely populated residential and commercial area namely Moolchand Marg. The local residents are facing health hazardous problems, have made complaints to the Municipal Council against the business of the petitioners. Therefore, the matter was considered and examined and it is found that the petitioners are selling Chicken/Mutton/Fish without no objection certificate and license, hence impugned notices were rightly issued to them . The no objection certificate granted to each petitioner by the Municipal Council was for the period of one year only and the said period has been expired. Now they are required to obtain fresh no objection certificate. Therefore, the petition is liable to be dismissed. [6] Shri Manoj Manav, learned counsel appearing for the petitioners submitted that the petitioners are engaged in the business of selling Chicken/Mutton/Fish from generation to generation since last 100 years which is their source of livelihood and they have right to do the business statutory and constitutional right to do the business for earning of livelihood. The same cannot be stopped without giving an opportunity of hearing and after following the due process available under the law. It is the duty of the Municipal Council to provide license and space for sale and purchase of Chicken/Mutton/Fish. If the Municipal Council is having objection in respect to the location where the petitioners are having the shops, then they must provide the alternate space/market for the said purpose and the petitioners are ready to shift .Their business which they are doing since last 100 years for surviving cannot abruptly be stopped. They should have been given breathing time to shift their business. [7] Shri V.K.Jain, learned Senior Counsel refuted the above arguments by submitting that since the petitioners are not having valid license and no objection certificate, therefore, the Municipal Council has rightly stopped them from selling Chicken/Mutton/Fish which is hazardous to health of local residents. They may be directed to apply for license and no objection certificate afresh and the Municipal Council shall consider the same in accordance with law. [8] That under Section 123 of the M. P. Municipalities Act, 1961 [in brief "the Act of 1961"], certain duties have been cast upon the Municipal Council to make adequate provisions by means or measures as provided under Clause (a) to (v). Sub-section 3 of Section 123 of the Act of 1961 provides that no suit for damage or for specific performance is maintainable against any Council or any officer or Councillor on the ground that any of the duty specified under sub-section 3 of Section 123 have not been performed. There are certain duties like lightning, public streets, cleaning, water facility, drainage and medical facility etc. which are compulsory in nature and it is the duty of the Municipal Council to provide for which a writ of mandamus can be issued to the Municipal Council. [10] Sub-section (1) (j) of Section 123 is reproduced below : " 123. Duties of Council.-- (1) In addition to the duties imposed upon it by or under this Act or any other enactment for the time being in force, it shall be the duty of a Council to undertake and make reasonable and adequate provision for the following matters within the limits of the Municipality, namely :- (a)............. (b)............. (c)............. (d)............. (e)............. (f)............. (g)............. (h)............. (i)............. (j) constructing, altering and maintaining public streets, culverts, Municipal boundary marks, markets, hats, salughter-houses, latrines, privies, urinals, drains, sewers, drainage works, sewerages works, baths, washing places, dringking fountains, tanks, wells, dams and the like;" [ 11 ] Section 3 (17) is reproduced below: "(17) "market or "bazar" means- (a) a place where persons assemble for the sale of meat, fish, fruit, vegetables, live-stock or any other articles of a perishable nature, whether or not there is any collection of shops, warehouses or stalls for the sale of other articles in such place; or (b) any place of trade than a place referred in sub- clause (a) where there is a collection of shops, warehouses or stalls; Mohammed Mustkim vs Urban Administration And Development ... on 15 January, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31428181/ 3 and shall include any "Hat" or place, where trade or business is carried on either weekly or bi-weekly or on certain fixed days of the week" [13] As per Section 260 of the Act of 1961, it shall be lawful for the Council to direct that no place other than a Municipal market shall be used for the sale of animals, meat, fish, fruit, vegetables or such other articles as the Council may prescribed. Section 260 of the Act of 1961 is reproduced below :- "260. Licensing markets.-- (1) It shall be lawful for the Council to direct that no place other than a Municipal market shall be used for the sale of animals, meat, fish, fruit, vegetables or such other articles as the Council may, with prior sanction of the prescribed authority, specify in this behalf except under and in accordance with the conditions of a licence from the Council which may, at its direction from time to time, grant, suspend, withhold or withdraw such licence either generally or in individual cases. (2) Whoever uses or permits the use of any place contrary to such direction or without the licence required as aforesaid, or in contravention of any of the conditions of during the suspension or after the withdrawal of such licence, shall be punished with fine which may extend to fifty rupees. (3) Upon a conviction being obtained in respect of any place under sub-section (2), the Magistrate shall, on the application of the Chief Municipal Officer or any officer authorized by him but not otherwise, order such place to be closed, and thereupon appoint persons or take other steps to prevent such place being so used; and every person who so uses or permits the use of a place after it has been so ordered to be closed, shall be punished with fine which may extend to five rupees of each day during which he continues so to use, or permits such use of, the place after it has been so ordered to be closed." [14] Under Section 268 of the Act of 1961, no person shall sell or offer or exposes for sale at any place within the Municipality, like animal or any meat except under and in accordance with the conditions of a licence granted by the Council. [15] Under sub-section (3) of Section 268, the provisions of sub-section (2) shall apply to sale of any such article from any house or shop, the Council is having discretion from time to time, grant, suspend, withhold or withdraw such licences. Under sub-section (5) whoever uses the premises or permits the use of any place without the licence, shall be punishable with find. [16] That section 358 gives power to the Municipal Council to frame by laws consistent with the provisions of the Act and the Rules for carrying out the provisions and intention of this Act.
